name: בַּעַל חָנָן
summary: בַּעַל “lord, owner”, the title of the Canaanite god, with the verb חָנַן. Borne by Baal-hanan son of Achbor, one of the kings of Edom “before any king reigned over the sons of Israel” (Gen 36:31, 38–39; 1Ch 1:49–50), and Baal-hanan the Gederite, David's overseer of the olive and sycamore trees in the Shephelah (1Ch 27:28).

evidence.note: “Shaul died, and בַּעַל חָנָן son of Achbor reigned in his place.”
“These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the sons of Israel.”
“Over the olive trees and the sycamores in the Shephelah, Baal-hanan the Gederite.”

note: Takes b.ci.af (5 tokens), BDB's key under בעל; the database also files the חָנָן of these verses under h.dz.ag (hanan) by spelling. The Punic ḥnbʿl (Hannibal, “grace of Baal”) is the same two words in the other order. For the Edomite the בַּעַל is the god; for David's Gederite it may be the title “lord”, used of Yahweh in Hos 2:18; not decided.
